steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir ground beef in the hot skillet until browned and crumbly, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and discard grease. Stir in spaghetti sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Combine cottage cheese, 2 cups of mozzarella cheese, eggs, 1/2 of the grated Parmesan cheese, dried parsley, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.

Spread 3/4 cup of sauce in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Cover with 3 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 3/4 cups of cheese mixture, and 1/4 cup sauce; repeat layers once more. Top with remaining 3 noodles, sauce, mozzarella, and Parmesan cheese. Pour 1/2 cup water along the edges of the dish. Cover tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes. Uncover and bake for an additional 10 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This easy lasagna recipe is made with lean ground beef, three types of cheese, and a jar of spaghetti sauce for a hearty, family-pleasing meal.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Lasagna

review.reviewBody: Very good. Indeed, the amount of cheese mixture is WAY too much for this recipe. I used 1 15-oz. containter of ricotta with same amount of eggs, mozzarella, parm, and replacing dried parsley with about 4 tbs fresh, and I replaced the 1/2 c. water with 1/4 c. water and 1/4 c. red wine. Very rich and tasty. However, a word to the wise: I unwisely chose to use 1/2 lb. lean ground beef with 1/2 lb. sausage. I think this would be a good decision if.. and I do mean ONLY IF... you have access to good spicy Italian-style sausage. Do not use "country" sausage or any sausage with a sweet base. Our local store had sausage, but it's flavored with sage and maple. Good with eggs. Bad with lasagne. Other than that, very simple, comparatively quick, little mess and rather tasty. I would, in the future, try it with a little garlic, some fresh basil, a dash of oregano, and maybe some cooked shrooms added in. I wouldn't use fresh shrooms, as it may make the dish too squishy and cause it to not "stand up" as a lasagne should. Definitnely worth a try with some tweaking.

This recipe saved the day when I had 5 college kids drop by for dinner unexpectedly. I used the "no-boil" lasagna noodles, mild Italian sausage instead of hamburg, and 60 ounces of spaghetti sauce, leaving out the water. I also layered in some fresh baby spinach leaves. It was a big hit!! Thanks!!

My husbands absolute favorite thing to eat is lasagna and I've been looking for an easy to make lasagna recipe- paticularly one where I didn't have to boil the noodles and one I could use store bought sauce. He's a pretty tough lasagna critic and he liked it alot. This was so easy to make and I'm glad I finally found an easy recipe to satisfy my husband's lasagna needs. The only change I made to the recipe was using ricotta cheese instead of cottage cheese- it turned out great!

Cooked in 9x12 disposable pan with 3" sides. Tall pan allowed for expansion of liquids (no spills). I kept the foil on top for 50 mins - making sure the noodles were done - and they were. Left foil off for 10 mins at 400 deg to brown. Left on counter for 10 mins where it tightened up considerably. I added 1/2 chopped yellow onion, and 3 cloves crushed garlic to heated pan, added 1 lb hot Italian sausage for a mellow kick. I used 8oz organic ricotta (no carrageenan) for cheese mix and it sufficed for two thin layers - could use more. Poured 1/4 cup red wine along edge. Result was delicious - everyone commented on flavor and said noodles were done! I'm a harsh critic of my own cooking and I liked this lasagna. Will make it again.

Delicious! You don't need to pre-cook regular lasagna noodles, or add the extra water; as long as you cover the noodles in sauce, they'll be cooked perfectly. I didn't add the water and I made it with regular white flour noodles AND gluten free noodles and everyone loved it! I also used half cottage cheese and half ricotta. I'm going to try adding in shredded zucchini next time. Delicious and easy! :)

Hi everyone! 1) Use more sauce instead of water. I omit the water all together and use 2-24 oz of spaghetti sauce (original and meat flavor sauce). 2) Use ricotta cheese. It’s thicker and more dense than cottage cheese. Yes, I did all 32 oz. 3) Layer goes like this: sauce to layer bottom of pan, noodles, ricotta mix, sauce. Then noodles, ricotta mix, sauce. Then noodles, ricotta mix, sauce and a whole lot of mozzarella cheese to top it all. At the end of cooking, we will put this to the broiler and get that crispy cheese up top 4) Cook at 350° for one hour. Then 10 minutes to the broiler. 5) I use regular Barelli’s uncooked lasagna noodles. Nothing fancy and still came out soft and delicious 6) Flavor the ricotta mix OR the meat sauce !!! Use a generous amount of seasoning to either. The sauce I used did not have too much sodium so the meat sauce mixture was lacking some umami. Luckily I salt up the ricotta so that kicks up the flavor a bit. Good luck to the home cooks!!! Remember, we tried our best and at the end of the day, that’s the best we could do :)

Fried the beef with 2 tsps of garlic and one finely chopped onion. Added 2 teaspoons of Italiano seasoning when I added in 1 1/2 bottles of spaghetti sauce (1 bottle is not enough to soften noodles). I added a generous amount of fresh spinach on top of the final layer of sauce. Topped it off with the final layer of noodles and sprinkled mozzarella generously on top. I omitted the salt and the pepper; with the Italiano seasoning and the garlic it wasn't necessary. I also added the half cup of water poured around the sides - a must! To keep it from bubbling over I tore a large piece of tinfoil and placed the pan on top of the foil and then brought it all up to wrap it like a present, that did the trick and the little juice that bubbled out caught nicely in the tinfoil.

I used this recipe to make the first lasagna in my life. It came out so good and super easy to follow. Notes: Use 15 noodles in 13x9 pan. Uses half a green pepper and half a white onion finely chopped while cooking meat, add spices, garlic powder, oregano, crushed red pepper, parsley, salt, pepper, don't drain. Use two 24 oz cans Hunts pasta sauce, simmer for 10 minutes. Don't add water in final stage of recipe. Cook at 360° for 55 minutes. Remove lid cook for another 15 minutes.
I tried this but very soupy. I made it again and didn't add the water around outside edges and it was perfect!!!

Loved it! I haven't made lasagna in years. When I did make it, I never boiled the noodles. Fast forward to this Christmas eve and a request from my youngest who was flying in from AZ. My favorite brand of gf pasta is Tinkyada but I saw a rice/corn blend from Barilla, which I picked up instead. I used 1/2 ricotta and 1/2 cottage plus two jars of sauce. I look at recipes for suggestions and break off with what I have on hand and what I know from past experience. I season the meat and add the water into the sauce. I found a shaved blend of asiago, parmesan, and Romano with which I am a little heavy handed. I ended up having more cheese blend so I made a second, smaller dish. Everyone loved it. Today is the 3rd time I've made it and I'm using beyond meat and since I'm low on noodles, I have a two layers of baby spinach. Hoping it is just as good!

My husband said it was the best lasagne he ever tasted. I used ricotta cheese. Added another egg. One and a half jars of Rao sauce. Added some left over Italian sausage to ground beef with a large clove of minced garlic. Only 6 tsp water. One each into the corners and in the middle on either side of the pan. Pasta came out fully cooked. I used 5 each layer.
This is a great recipe! I used ricotta cheese instead of cottage cheese . This is my new go to lasagna recipe🙂

I had leftover Spaghetti sauce, which consisted of 1/2 ground Beef, 1/2 ground Pork, diced whole Onion carmelized, several cloves of minced Garlic, 1/3 c Dark Brown Sugar, several dashes of Italian Seasoning, and Granulated Garlic, with two jars of store bought sauce. With so much leftover sauce I decided to make this Lasagna Recipe. I used 12 lasagna noodles that I boiled first. Cheese mixture was exactly the same. The mozzarella that our store had was a block of low-moisture part skim. Freshly grated BelgGioiso parmesean, not Kraft! Fresh Basil chopped. Sprinkles of Granulated Garlic, Salt and Pepper. I sprayed the inside part of the foil with cooking spray to keep the cheese from sticking to it, then refrigerated it overnight. So Baking time extended to about 65-70 mins. When baking with the foil off, 15 mins was not enough, extended another 15 mins. There wasn’t enough browning and the temp was sitting at 150°. Bumped the temp to 375° and baked 10 mins more. Came out amazing. Next time I make this, I think I’ll use half cottage cheese and the other half will be Ricotta. Instead of ground pork, I’d like to use Ground Sweet Italian Sausage. More fresh Basil, maybe even dried to the cheese mixture, as well as Italian Seasoning, and a bit more Salt & Pepper.
It is so good that my husband texted me from his job and asked if we could have the leftovers for supper the following night.That is a rarity in itself.
This was amazing! I was in too much pain to spend time customizing, so the only change I made was to add fresh mushrooms. Full of flavor and really filling.

My family raved about this lasagna. I added garlic, onion and chili powder as well as 1/4 c. sugar to the sauce. I also added about 4T Worcestershire sauce. To the cheese mixture I added an extra egg. I used oven ready lasagna noodles.
I thought it was delicious and light with ground chicken. I will add more herbs and less salt next time.

Followed the recipe to a T. Only thing I did different was add about half the recommended water after reading comments and that seems to have worked well. Otherwise it turned out fantastic. I will make this again for sure!
Simple and good for family night.
Very easy recipe, the only thing (and I can't believe I'm saying this) , there is too much cheese.. Maybe it's just me... 😁
